items.title: ArtStation Will Block AI Crawlers From Scraping Artists' Work
items.excerpt: ArtStation has enabled NoAI protection for new and existing uploads and introduced safeguards against AI crawlers, while admitting its current AI content filters are insufficient.
items.why: The default portfolio home for game artists just changed its scraping posture — this is where concept and environment artists' consent settings actually live.

items.title: How Agents 404's Devs Prototyped With AI and Gained 120K Wishlists in Two Months
items.excerpt: PlayHero founder Anton Slashcev explains how the AI tool Bezi helped his team prototype Agents 404 in one month, why core systems stayed hand-authored, and where human technical expertise is still essential.
items.why: A rare concrete before/after on AI-assisted prototyping: what the tool did, what the team refused to hand over, and the measurable market result.

items.title: DLSS 5 Can Be Jammed Into Almost Any Game Now — Neural-Rendered People in FM26
items.excerpt: Nvidia's generative DLSS 5 face/detail layer can now be forced into games it was never shipped for, letting players run neural-rendered characters in titles like Football Manager 26.
items.why: A generative model is now overriding the art direction of games at runtime, outside the studio's control — a new category of visual-integrity problem for art teams.

items.title: Steam Week in Review: A Touch of AI Is All It Takes to Trigger Backlash
items.excerpt: A promising new indie fell afoul of 'slop skeptics' on Steam, showing how little AI-touched asset work it now takes to derail a launch's reception.
items.why: Practical risk calibration for anyone shipping AI-assisted art: the audience penalty is triggered by trace amounts, not by scale of use.

items.title: Nvidia Announces Ray-Traced Nanite, Native Anti-Cheat and DLSS 4.5 at Gamescom 2026
items.excerpt: Nvidia used Gamescom to detail a wave of developer-facing updates across DLSS, RTX and GeForce Now, including ray-traced Nanite and DLSS 4.5.
items.why: Neural rendering is moving from upscaler to core pipeline feature — it changes what technical artists can budget for in look-dev.

items.title: No Man's Sky Fan Adds DLSS 5 — Hello Games Programmer Worries It Could Ruin Its Look and Feel
items.excerpt: A modder pushed Nvidia's DLSS 5 AI filter into No Man's Sky, prompting a Hello Games programmer to warn the generative layer could erase the game's deliberately stylised look.
items.why: A working developer articulating exactly how a post-process AI model destroys authored style — the clearest art-direction argument in the DLSS 5 fight.

items.title: DLSS 5 Can Now Be Used To AI-Sloppify Real People
items.excerpt: Users have pointed DLSS 5's generative detail pass at live webcam feeds, turning real faces into the same smoothed, over-rendered look the filter applies to game characters.
items.why: Shows the aesthetic signature of a real-time generative filter in isolation — a useful visual vocabulary lesson for anyone judging AI-touched imagery.

items.title: Video Game Companies Keep Trying To Bait And Switch Us With AI
items.excerpt: 1666: Amsterdam, Blood of Dawnwalker and others claim AI assets didn't make the final game — but that doesn't mean the projects were AI-free.
items.why: Unpicks the emerging PR pattern of 'no AI in the shipped build' — a disclosure-language problem every studio comms and design lead now has to answer for.

items.title: Nvidia's Face-Changing Gen-AI DLSS 5 Releases for One Game, and Seems to Tank Frame Rates
items.excerpt: Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 generative tech launches on 50-series GeForce cards and GeForce Now with NBA 2K27, with early reports of significant frame-rate cost.
items.why: The first shipped consumer generative rendering feature — and the first hard data on what it costs in performance.

items.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Won't Have Microtransactions or Generative AI at Launch
items.excerpt: Rockstar told Kinda Funny Games that Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch without microtransactions or generative AI, though its Ultimate Edition still gates some content.
items.why: The most expensive game ever made is publicly opting out of generative AI — a benchmark statement for every studio's own policy.

items.title: No, the Humankind 2 Announcement Trailer Wasn't Made With Gen-AI
items.excerpt: Viewers flagged the Humankind 2 reveal trailer as AI-generated; the studio responded to explain how the sequence was actually made.
items.why: False-positive AI accusations are now a real production risk — stylistic choices are being read as machine output, and studios need a defence.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 5 Releases This Week With NBA 2K27, AI 'Yassification' Filter and All
items.excerpt: Nvidia's controversial generative graphics tech debuted on September 3rd with NBA 2K27, with early looks focused on how it restyles player faces.
items.why: Names the aesthetic failure mode precisely — generative enhancement drifting toward a homogenised 'beautified' face, regardless of the character design.

items.title: Penguin Colony's Release Date Trailer Gave Me a GenAI Fright — But There's No Cause for Concern
items.excerpt: A critic's first read of Penguin Colony's trailer was 'this looks AI-generated' — then the actual production process turned out to be hand-made.
items.why: A field note on how AI suspicion is reshaping how audiences read visual style — and how quickly a trailer can be misjudged.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction Is Out Now, Upping Shadow Quality
items.excerpt: Nvidia released DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, an upgraded version of its neural path-tracing denoiser that improves shadow quality and material illumination.
items.why: The uncontroversial half of neural rendering: a learned denoiser that raises lighting fidelity without touching authored art.

items.title: DLSS 5 Finally Has a Use Case — Making Cyberpunk 2077 Genuinely Dystopian
items.excerpt: Players are applying DLSS 5's generative face pass to Cyberpunk 2077, where the uncanny, over-smoothed result accidentally suits the game's themes.
items.why: A reminder that a generative filter is itself a style choice — it can reinforce or fight a game's authored tone, and studios don't get to opt in.

items.title: ByteBrew Brings Live Operations Into App Developers' AI Workflows
items.excerpt: ByteBrew is folding live-ops into agentic AI workflows, aiming to close the loop from player-behaviour insight to in-game action without manual handoffs.
items.why: Live-ops agents start making balance and content decisions that used to be a designer's call — worth watching where the authorship line lands.
